:JUDGMENT:
This petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 09.10.2022 wherein the petitioner has sought for compensation with respect to the death of Sri Shreyas due to the impact of the accident.
2. Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner is the grandfather of deceased Shreyas who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 09.10.2022 due to the rash and negligent driving of SCCH 15 3 MVC No.6348/2022 the driver of the respondent's mini bus.

It is submitted that on 09.10.2022 at about 7.00 a.m., when Shreyas was proceeding in his motorcycle and when he reached near Joshi Nursing School, Ullala main road, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the Mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AF-7513 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle) drove in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life with high speed and lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the motorcycle from opposite side.
Due to this impact, Shreyas sustained severe head injury and died on the spot.

Consequently, on 09.10.2022 FIR No.0210/2022 was registered with the Kamakshipalya Traffic Police station under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and charge sheet was filed under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.3(1), 181, 5, 180 of MV Act.
The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the mini bus.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 27 years and working at Meru Info Solutions and earning SCCH 15 4 MVC No.6348/2022 Rs.27,707/-
per month and he was the sole bread earner and had good future prospects.
Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioner has lost love, affection and support which has caused mental agony to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has claimed compensation of Rs.95,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
3. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 has remained absent and placed exparte.

sentences.text: The petitioner in support of his claim has in addition to describing the course of accident in line with the facts mentioned in the complaint has relied upon Ex.P1 to 10 documents.

Ex.P1 is the FIR registered against the driver of the offending vehicle on the basis of complaint given by one Rajesh on 09.10.2022 on same day of the accident which discloses that there is no delay in lodging the complaint.
In addition Ex.P3 is the statement given by the petitioner before the police.
Ex.P4 spot mahazar and sketch speaks about the spot of the accident.

The said document discloses that the accident has taken place on old ring road towards Mangalore PU college and driver of the offending vehicle drove in a rash and negligent manner and in the process of overtaking another vehicle all of a sudden turned the bus towards right side and hit motorist, resulting in the accident.
Ex.P5 is the Inquest report and Ex.P6 PM report discloses that the deceased succumbed to the injuries due to the impact of the accident.
Ex.P9 reveal damages caused to both SCCH 15 8 MVC No.6348/2022 the vehicles which shows their involvement in the accident.

Ex.P10 is the charge sheet filed after completion of investigation against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offenses under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.3(1), 181, 5, 180 of IMV Act on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid Driving license as on the date of the accident.
The charge sheet materials discloses that the driver of the offending vehicle went to overtake another vehicle which was going ahead and dashed the motorcycle resulting in the accident.
Hence, these documents satisfactorily establish that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
10. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned Pw1 is cross examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 and it is admitted that PW.1 has not seen the accident.
He came to know about the accident from his grand son's friend.

He has denied that the deceased himself skidded,
resulting in the accident.
He further deposed that parents of the deceased have already expired in the year 2000 and deceased was bachelor.

Except suggestion that the accident has taken place due to the SCCH 15 9 MVC No.6348/2022 negligence of the deceased nothing much is elicited in the cross- examination of PW.1 to prove that the accident took place due to the negligence of the deceased.
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.

The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and Sec.3(1), 181, 5, 180 of MV Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of medical records there is no dispute regarding the death occurred in the above accident.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that death occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in favour of the petitioner and in the 'Affirmative'.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:
It is stated in the Petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that the Petitioner is the grandfather of deceased Shreyas.
To prove his relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has SCCH 15 10 MVC No.6348/2022 relied on Ex.P13 & 14 i.e., the Aadhaar cards of the Petitioner and deceased.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioner and the deceased.
Hence, he has a right to apply for compensation due to death of his grandson Shreyas in the road traffic accident.
12. The Petitioner is the grandfather of the deceased, being the legal representative of deceased Shreyas has a right to apply for compensation.

As the Petitioner is the legal heir of deceased Shreyas and also he has proved that the death of the Shreyas is due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle he is entitled for just compensation.
Hence I answer Issue No 2 in the Affirmative.

13. Issue No.3: Computation of compensation under the various heads is assessed as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Age factor:
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of SCCH 15 11 MVC No.6348/2022 the deceased is shown as 27 years.
Ex.P-13 is the Aadhaar card which shows that the date of birth of the deceased is 18.10.1995.
The alleged accident has taken place on 09.10.2022.
Hence, by considering Ex.P13, the age of the deceased is taken as 27 years as on the date of the accident.
14. Income and avocation:
It is stated in the evidence that deceased was working at Meru Info Solutions and earning Rs.24,707/- per month.

In order to prove the income and avocation the petitioner has adduced the evidence of PW2, who is the HR Manager of Meru Info Solutions and he has produced the pay slips of the deceased from January 2022 to October 2022 along with attendant register and Form No.16.

On perusal of these documents it discloses that the deceased was appointed as customer support Executive in Meru Info Solutions dated 30.11.2016 and Ex.P20 to 29 are the payslips of the deceased and as per the pay slip of September 2022 he was having salary of Rs.22,996/- per month.

Furthermore PW1 has got examined the HR Manager of Meru Info solutions as PW2 and he has deposed that the deceased was employee in their company and was drawing SCCH 15 12 MVC No.6348/2022 a salary of Rs.22.996/-.

15. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121

sentences.text:
Relevant part of the judgment at paras 18- 19 is reproduced hereunder:
"18.

The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
There will be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependant family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the deceased."

22. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.

However the respondent No 2 has disputed the liability on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle did not valid driving SCCH 15 21 MVC No.6348/2022 license and hence there is a breach of the policy conditions.

The respondent Insurance company has got examined RW.1 to 4,
RW.1 is the investigation officer and has deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have valid driving license as on the date of the accident.

Further RW.3 FDA, Nelamangala RTO has deposed that as per the DL extract Ex.R4 there was license only to drive vehicle upto 7500 GVW capacity and the driver of the offending vehicle did not have license to drive vehicle of 42 seating capacity and 9600GVW capacity and hence it is submitted that the offending vehicle did not have valid driving license as on the date of the accident.

23. On this point the respondent insurance company has also got examined the Legal Manager as RW4 and he also deposed that though the insurance policy was valid as on the date of the accident however in view of the violation of the policy conditions, no liability can be fastened on the insurance company.

24. A careful glance of the extract of driving license marked as ExR4 discloses that the driver has DL to drive LMV (NT) and LMVCAB (TR) and the driving license was renewed from time to SCCH 15 22 MVC No.6348/2022 time.
Hence the pivotal question is as to whether the driver did not have valid driving to drive the offending vehicle.

Admittedly the offending vehicle is a passenger bus with 42 seating capacity and the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license only for LMVCAB (TR)
which does not include the offending vehicle and hence there is a breach of the policy conditions and the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner of the vehicle.

25. However the evidence discloses that it is not a case of absence of driving license to drive any type of vehicle but it is case of not having effective driving license to drive the offending vehicle in question and hence though there is a breach of the policy conditions it shall entitle the insurance company a right to seek recovery of the compensation paid to the claimants from the owner of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the insurance company would contend that the accident having occurred after the amendment and hence the principle of pay and recovery is not applicable.
However there is no clear provision by way of amendment to indicate that the said principle is no longer in existence.
If the SCCH 15 23 MVC No.6348/2022 legislature intended to wipe out the said principle it would have made a clear provision to that effect.

Furthermore the contract of insurance is between the insurer and the insured and the intention of making statutory third party insurance is to compensate the road accident victims and their remedy cannot be abridged on the ground on of breach of policy conditions.
Hence they are entitled to obtain compensation from respondent no 2 who in turn will have to recover the same from the insured.
Hence the Respondent No.1 being owner of the vehicle is liable to pay the compensation.
However Respondent No.2 will have to deposit the compensation amount and thereafter recover the same from Respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
27. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.36,12,800/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner SCCH 15 24 MVC No.6348/2022 against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.36,12,800/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

However, the Respondent No.2 being the Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest as stated above within 60 days from the date of the Award and thereafter recover the same from the Respondent No.1 through due process of law.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There is no material on record which suggests falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW.1 as to the facts and circumstances surrounding cause of the accident.
The fact that the driver of the offending vehicle has already been charge sheeted for the offenses under Sec.279 and 304(A) of IPC and Sec.3(1), 181, 5, 180 of MV Act itself is strong circumstance to support the oral testimony of PW.1.
The certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, IMV report and Spot mahazar also corroborate the oral testimony of PW.1.
In view of the said discussion it is satisfactorily established that death occurred on account of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
Income is not confined to receipts from business only and means periodical receipts from one's work, lands,
investments, etc. Secy. to the Board of Revenue, Income Tax v. Al. Ar. Rm.
Arunachalam Chettiar & Bros. [AIR 1921 Mad 427] Ref. Vulcun Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Corpn. of Madras [AIR 1930 Mad 626 (2)].'
21.
If the dictionary meaning of the word 'income' is taken to its logical conclusion, it should include those benefits, either in terms of money or otherwise, which are taken into consideration for the purpose of payment of income tax or professional tax although some elements thereof may or may not be taxable or would have been otherwise taxable but for the exemption conferred thereupon under the statute.
To the same effect is the decision of this Court in Oriental Insurance Company Limited v. Ram Prasad Varma [(2009) 2 SCC 712 : (2009) 1 SCC (Cri) 853 : (2009) 1 Scale 598].
7.
We, therefore, are of the opinion that "dearness allowance"
and "house rent allowance" payable to the deceased should have been included for determining the income of the deceased and consequently the amount of compensation."
15. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.
Moving forward with the Point of future prospects,
the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.
Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 40% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the deceased is self- employed and was below the age of 40 years.
16.
At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his grandfather.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.
In this Petition, the deceased was aged 27 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the SCCH 15 17 MVC No.6348/2022 income has to be added.
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 17.
However the respondent No 2 has disputed the liability on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle did not valid driving SCCH 15 21 MVC No.6348/2022 license and hence there is a breach of the policy conditions.
25. However the evidence discloses that it is not a case of absence of driving license to drive any type of vehicle but it is case of not having effective driving license to drive the offending vehicle in question and hence though there is a breach of the policy conditions it shall entitle the insurance company a right to seek recovery of the compensation paid to the claimants from the owner of the offending vehicle.
If the SCCH 15 23 MVC No.6348/2022 legislature intended to wipe out the said principle it would have made a clear provision to that effect.
Furthermore the contract of insurance is between the insurer and the insured and the intention of making statutory third party insurance is to compensate the road accident victims and their remedy cannot be abridged on the ground on of breach of policy conditions.
Hence they are entitled to obtain compensation from respondent no 2 who in turn will have to recover the same from the insured.
